title: Elastic microcredit layer for transient borrowing across misaligned quota epochs
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Tenants with different reset cadences (midnight local, monthly anchors, and reserved pool windows) currently experience short-term hard throttles when their local epoch boundary diverges from the reserved-capacity allocation window. This causes poor UX for bursty workloads and generates noisy invoice adjustments when we reconcile usage post-reset.

Goal: Introduce a transient borrowing layer ("microcredit" layer) that allows safe, observable short-term borrowing across epoch boundaries with deterministic reconciliation during the next anchor alignment. The system must guarantee no permanent quota inflation, provide auditable ledger entries for billing, and be reversible in case of migration rollback.

High-level design:
- Per-tenant microcredit ledger: small floats of temporary credits (configurable cap, e.g., up to 10% of monthly quota or X tokens) that can be consumed when the tenant's primary epoch has exhausted quota but the tenant is within a reservation window.
- Global fallback pool: a bounded pool to serve transient demand spikes for tenants without reserved carry capacity; used only when global headroom exists.
- Deterministic reconciliation: on next reset boundary, borrowings are reconciled against the tenant's usage and reserved commitment; system either deducts from next epoch or triggers a prorated invoice adjustment for reserved customers based on policy.
- Safety controls: per-tenant caps, slow-fill backoff, instant hard-fail for tenants flagged for abuse, and feature-flag gating for gradual rollout.
- Telemetry: new dashboards showing microcredit issuance, borrow/repay rates, and per-tenant reconciliation outcomes to ensure no loss in billing correctness.

Data model changes (summary):
- microcredit_ledger table (tenant_id, epoch_anchor, issued_amount, consumed_amount, refunded_amount, status, created_at, reconciled_at)
- migration will be append-only and replay-friendly to allow reprocessing if reconciliation job is rerun.

Trade-offs considered:
- Allowing temporary borrowing improves availability but complicates invoicing; we prefer deterministic ledger reconciliation over retroactive subjective adjustments.
- Bounded microcredits reduce fiscal exposure but may still leave corner cases; we will tune caps and provide clear customer-facing documentation.

Out-of-scope: cross-tenant transfers, long-term credit rolling beyond one epoch, automated refunds without manual review for certain reserved-plan customers (requires billing legal sign-off).
acceptance_criteria: Microcredit issuance is limited by per-tenant cap and global cap and respects feature-flag off behavior (no issuance).
Reconciliation job runs idempotently and produces an auditable ledger entry for every borrow/repay event.
No unbounded negative ledger states after reconciliation; system either deducts from next epoch or produces a chargeable adjustment for reserved customers according to policy.
Rollout gated behind a runtime feature flag and can be disabled without manual DB rollbacks.
Dashboards display issuance/repayment counts and show <1% unexpected variance in billing simulations during canary runs.

Schema migration: add microcredit_ledger table and index strategy (owner: Eng-Infra)
Runtime: implement issuance/consume APIs in quota service with safety checks (owner: quota-service team)
Reconciliation: implement idempotent reconciliation job and regression tests (owner: billing-worker)
Telemetry: add Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards for issuance/repayment/reconciliations (owner: observability)
E2E: create integration tests that simulate misaligned windows and reserved pool interactions (owner: qa)
Load test: run cluster-scale soak to validate latency/throughput under burst patterns (owner: perf)
Rollout: gradual canary over 5% -> 25% -> 100% with manual checkpoints and rollback playbook (owner: SRE)
Docs: update public billing docs and internal runbook describing reconciliation and customer-facing outcomes (owner: Docs)
PRs: land implementation behind feature flag and open follow-up for billing automation (owner: assignee)
